title: Stepdown Orchestra — warmup & canary journal (personal notes)
content:
Quick private scratchpad for the upcoming model flip (v2.14 -> v2.15) and the stepdown/stepup choreography. Not a final runbook — capture of thoughts, rough checks and telemetry queries I want to validate before handing to oncall.

Purpose:
- Move traffic from v2.14 (baseline) to v2.15 (quantized+kv-fix) with minimal customer-visible regressions.
- Validate that latency p50/p95 delta is within SLO and error budget impact is negligible.
- Have a deterministic stepdown path for fast pinback if instability observed.

High-level phases (quick sketch):
- PREP (today): pin v2.14 Canary tag for internal users; warm caches with replay of last 24h low-latency traces.
- MICRO-CANARY (T+0): 0.1% traffic, 30m min, sanity checks.
- SCALED-CANARY (T+1): 1% traffic, 1h min, add metric watchlist.
- WAVE-RAMP (T+2): 10% -> 25% -> 50% increments, 30m each if green.
- SWEEP (T+3): full cutover or slow-drip to 100% depending on telemetry.
- STEP-DOWN (escape): immediate pinback to v2.14 and route heavy clients to dedicated fallback while we triage.

Pinning strategy notes:
- Use route-level pinning for high-risk customers: set config.routeOverrides[customer] -> model:v2.14 for top 20 revenue buckets during the first 24h.
- Global default route moves to v2.15 at 50% wave only after two consecutive green windows.
- Deploy flag: rollout.enable-stepdown-automatic = true (allows automatic revert if error-rate threshold exceeded).

Preflight checklist (things I want green before any traffic shift):
- Perf: p50 delta <= +8ms, p95 delta <= +40ms on same hardware profile. Query: metrics.query("p50,p95 by model where model in (v2.14,v2.15) and region='us-west' last_1h").
- Errors: 5xx rate baseline <= 0.3% and v2.15 not > baseline + 0.2%. Query: metrics.query("error_rate by model last_30m").
- Tokenization/regression: run eval set small-prompts.json (50 prompts) — BLEU/ROUGE quick diff. CI job: gh-action/evals/quick-smoke.
- KV cache sanity: run internal trace for long-context prompts (2 examples from INT-620) and confirm cache hit rates look similar.
- Canary infra: ensure autoscaler target buffer has +20% capacity headroom. Ops check: infra/ASG-health last_4h = healthy.

Micro-canary watchers (who to call):
- Primary oncall: Ravi Menon (pager), Backup: Leah Kim.
- Product liaison: Mia Torres (for behavioral regressions).
- Infra: SRE lead: Jonas G. (for autoscaling anomalies).

Telemetry & alert triggers (initial):
- Hard stop: 5xx spike > 1% absolute for 5m. (Action: immediate pinback to v2.14 global + notify all).
- Soft stop: p95 increase > 80ms vs baseline for 10m. (Action: pause ramp, hold & investigate).
- Quality drift: eval-smoke BLEU drop > 5 point or obvious hallucination pattern on test set. (Action: pause, run narrower evalset, consider partial pin).
- Latency tail: GPU mem pressure > 85% sustained 10m. (Action: throttle new canaries, scale pool).

Quick rollback commands I keep near-hand:
- Pin global: curl -X POST https://console.internal/redwood/api/pins -d '{"route":"default","model":"v2.14"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $__TOKEN'
- Route override for big accounts: POST /api/routes/override {customer_id: 12345, model: v2.14, until: +24h}
- Emergency: set rollout.enable-stepdown-automatic = false (to stop auto-bounces while triaging)

Open experiment ideas (note-to-self):
- Canary smoothing: instead of instant 0.1% -> 1% jump, use probabilistic sampling with per-client sticky seed to avoid cohort collisions.
- Gradual quantization ramp: test small-bundle of cold traffic against fully quantized model to see cold start penalties.

Loose timeline (proposal):
- Wed 2026-03-11: PREP + smoke on staging (done)
- Thu 2026-03-12: MICRO-CANARY 0.1% (monitor)
- Thu 2026-03-12 11:00 UTC: SCALED-CANARY 1% if green
- Fri 2026-03-13: WAVE-RAMP to 25% then weekend observation

Notes from today's run of evaluation:
- Quick-bleu: baseline 68.3 vs v2.15 67.9 (delta -0.4) — ok but keep eye on few prompts that dropped more.
- Latency p95 on small batch (n=100) increased from 320ms -> 365ms on A100; distribution shows heavier tail for certain long prompts. Likely kv-cache alignment issue.
- Infra logs: one transient enqueuing delay seen at 2026-03-11T16:02:14Z - root cause seems to be a cold-scheduler bug fixed in PR 872 (linked). Need to confirm fix in production path.

Action items (short):
- [ ] Ask SRE to warm scheduler pools for US clusters before micro-canary (Jonas).
- [ ] Add two long-context prompts to quick smoke set (Leah).
- [ ] Create a pinned fallback route for top-10 tenants (Ravi).
- [ ] Run canary for +2h longer than usual to capture tail variance (me).

Questions to resolve before full ramp:
- Is the kv-cache fix (PR 872) present in the same inference bundle customers will hit? (check deployment matrix).
- If we observe small but consistent BLEU swing, do we prefer smart-sampling of affected prompts or full revert? (tradeoff: user experience vs rollout momentum).

Rough postmortem checklist if we need to revert:
- Capture 30m of raw traces for both models for offline analysis.
- Dump KV cache diagnostics for one failing machine.
- Tag rollout timeline in incident timeline doc and link JIRA.

Random thoughts (brain-dump):
- Might be worth exposing a per-route quality gating metric so product can opt in for conservative behavior.
- Consider canary weighting by client revenue to reduce blast radius for the same traffic percent.

——
End of scratchpad. Keeping this here until I consolidate into the formal runbook. Will move to shared_drives/engineering/release-runbooks once validated.
